title: Southeast Asia’s digital economy to hit $368 billion
gist: Google, Temasek and Bain's 11th e-Conomy SEA report projects Southeast Asia's digital economy at $368B GMV in 2026 (+17%), on track for over $1T by 2035, with generative AI used by 243M people and a projected 60-fold rise in AI usage by 2030. Constraints include a ~3x data center capacity expansion, energy efficiency rules and the November 2026 ASEAN DEFA.

themes.theme: Size and growth of SEA digital economy

insights.claim: Southeast Asia's digital economy is projected to grow 17% YoY to $368B GMV in 2026 and exceed $1 trillion by 2035.
insights.speaker: Nitin Gajria
insights.so_what: The report is sponsored by Google, so projections carry an interest in AI-driven narratives, but the base figure is a useful regional sizing anchor.

insights.claim: Generative AI is used by 243 million Southeast Asians, 58% of the working population, and is scaling four times faster than the mobile internet rollout did.
insights.speaker: Nitin Gajria
insights.so_what: Adoption speed faster than mobile suggests rapid demand for compute and agent-based services regionally.
insights.quote: scaling four times faster than the rollout of the mobile internet

insights.claim: The report uses tokens as the benchmark for the AI economy and projects a 60-fold surge in regional AI usage over five years, driven by confidence in agentic commerce.
insights.speaker: Nitin Gajria
insights.so_what: Token volume as a metric links consumer behavior directly to inference demand, an input for data center and chip demand forecasts.

insights.claim: E-commerce is the anchor at $226B GMV (+18% YoY), and AI-personalized experiences are said to yield 10% higher conversions and order volume uplifts as large as 75%.
insights.speaker: Nitin Gajria
insights.so_what: Conversion-uplift claims are the economic case for retailers' AI spend, though they are unattributed to specific studies.
insights.locator: 1. AI is sustaining growth in every sector.

insights.claim: Online travel is $59B GMV (+10%), where search engines remain the top planning platform and generative AI has overtaken social media as the second-most used itinerary tool.
insights.speaker: Nitin Gajria
insights.so_what: AI displacing social media in trip planning shifts discovery power away from social platforms.

insights.claim: Online media reaches $44B revenue (+22%), the fastest-growing segment, with commerce media a $4B market and 10-20% engagement-quality uplift from personalization.
insights.speaker: Nitin Gajria
insights.so_what: Commerce media is a small but growing ad pool tied to AI-targeted feeds.

insights.claim: Mobility and food delivery reaches $40B GMV (+15%), and digital financial services $1,650B GTV (+16%), with AI used for routing, fraud detection and credit access.
insights.speaker: Nitin Gajria
insights.so_what: Financial services dwarfs other segments by transaction value, though GTV and GMV are not comparable revenue measures.

insights.claim: 72% of users already rely on features like price tracking, and 75% say they are willing to let AI agents autonomously compare prices and complete transactions.
insights.speaker: Nitin Gajria
insights.so_what: Stated willingness is not behavior, but high intent suggests agentic checkout could scale faster in SEA than in more skeptical markets.
insights.quote: 75% expressing willingness to let AI agents autonomously compare prices and complete transactions
insights.locator: 2. Consumer trust will help unlock the era of agentic commerce.

insights.claim: 62% report greater trust in AI tools than a year ago, citing proven track record (56%), familiarity (55%) and accuracy (53%).
insights.speaker: Nitin Gajria
insights.so_what: Trust is experience-driven, so a high-profile agent failure could reverse it.

insights.claim: Users' conditions for agentic features are privacy safeguards (44%), transparency about AI limits (36%) and reversibility of transactions (30%).
insights.speaker: Nitin Gajria
insights.so_what: Reversibility and privacy become product requirements and potential regulatory focus for payments and platforms.
insights.locator: To feel comfortable using new agentic capabilities

insights.claim: Supporting the 60-fold AI usage increase requires roughly 3x data center capacity expansion over five years, with AI workloads capturing a dominant share.
insights.speaker: Nitin Gajria
insights.so_what: A tripling of capacity implies significant power, land and chip demand across Singapore, Malaysia and neighbors.
insights.quote: ~3x expansion in data center capacity over the next five years

insights.claim: Singapore's binding Power Usage Effectiveness rules under the Digital Infrastructure Bill and Malaysia's CRESS clean energy supply model are cited as frameworks for next-generation facilities.
insights.speaker: Nitin Gajria
insights.so_what: Efficiency mandates and clean power access will be gating factors in where data centers are sited.

insights.claim: The ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement (DEFA), due in November 2026, is described as the world's first region-wide digital trade pact.
insights.speaker: Nitin Gajria
insights.so_what: A region-wide pact could ease cross-border data and digital trade, a potential catalyst for regional platforms.
insights.quote: the upcoming ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement (DEFA) in November 2026

insights.claim: The report says AI model running costs must keep falling and deliver clear practical value so businesses of all sizes can adopt agents sustainably.
insights.speaker: Nitin Gajria
insights.so_what: Inference unit economics are a stated bottleneck to broad SMB adoption.
insights.locator: Accelerated agentic adoption and sustainable economics
